summary:
GreenOrbit helps farmers and the water users' board of the Majes irrigated plain (Arequipa, Peru) decide what to sow when water is scarce. Majes is a desert farmed with canal water: about 334 million m³ arrive each year, satellites show plants and soil consume about 138, and the current crop mix would already need 78–99 % of the available water, leaving almost no margin for a dry year such as the strong El Niño forecast for 2027.

We built a web tool with two levels. The board sees whether the water reaches a crop mix and a map of where dry years hit hardest, from NASA MODIS greenness of every 5.4 ha pixel since 2013. Farmers pick the crops they can sow and their priorities (save water, protect soil, earn more) and get three-season rotations that follow agronomic rules, fit their water month by month, and explain why, including what we do not know. It supports decisions; it does not replace them.

GREENORBIT — WHAT TO PLANT SO THE WATER LASTS

Live demo: https://greenorbit-six.vercel.app

The app: https://greenorbit-six.vercel.app/app/

3D terrain: https://greenorbit-six.vercel.app/app/flyover.html?tour=1

API docs: https://greenorbit-six.vercel.app/docs

Source code: https://github.com/Olhes/Adapting-Farms-NASA

Video: [YouTube link]

THE PROBLEM

The Majes plateau (Arequipa, Peru) is a desert. Everything that grows there arrives through one canal: about 334 million m³ a year. Nearly half the irrigated area is a single thirsty crop, alfalfa. When deliveries drop, the same crops no longer fit in the same months. Farmers and the Water Users Board need to know, before sowing, whether the water will be enough.

WHAT IT DOES

- Farmer view: pick what you grow today and set tprotect the soil, earn more). GreenOrbit generates every three-season rotation, discards those that break agronomic rotation rules, and ranks the rest. Your current practicalways shown for comparison.

- Water, month by month: each rotation shows whether it fits the roughly 21,000 m³ per hectare a year that arrive, in a nyear and in a dry-year stress case (84 % of norma

- Your plot from space: tap the map to see the MODIS pixel that contains your plot, its greenness (NDVI), its water use (how it did in past dry years.

- Water Users Board view: demand of the whole district's crop mix against the water available, with adjustable assumption- Real 3D terrain: NASA SRTM relief, Sentinel-2 ivers from OpenStreetMap, and the irrigated MODISpixels on top. - Every recommendation explains why it wins, what missing. Interface in Spanish and English.

KEY FINDING

With today's crop mix, crops ask for between 260 and 331 million m³ a year, against 334 delivered. In the dry-year stressonly about 280 arrive, so the high estimate no lo

NASA AND PARTNER DATA

NASA MODIS MOD13Q1 (NDVI, 250 m) and MOD16A3GF (evapotranspiration, 500 m), 2013–2025; NASA POWER (climate for reference evapotranspiration); NASA SRTM (terrain); USGS SS EOX; Autodema canal deliveries at Pitay,2013–2025; Midagri yields, farm-gate prices and sowing dates; FAO-56 and FAO-29.

HOW WE CHECKED IT

- Our NDVI and ET extraction matches NASA AppEEARzero difference; ET correlation 0.999.

- Our Penman-Monteith implementation reproduces FAO-56 Example 18 (3.88 mm/day).

- Water demand is reported as a range between two and Penman-Monteith), not as a single number.

- We tested a predictive yield model (CatBoost, leave-one-year-out). It did not beat each crop's usual yield, so we do not use

it.

- 146 automated tests cover the data, the water model, the rotation rules and the API.

LIMITS

Water figures are order-of-magnitude estimates. Nxcept alfalfa, so income is gross revenue. Nomeasured soil salinity per plot. Water per plot uses the district average, because per-plot delivery records are not public.

Satellite pixels are 5.4 ha, larger than many plocase built from the lowest delivery seen in eachmonth, harsher than any single recorded year. GreenOrbit supports the decision; it does not replace it.

TOOLS

Python, FastAPI, NumPy, pandas, rasterio, MicrosoavaScript, Leaflet, three.js, Tailwind CSS,pytest, Vercel.
